blocks.text: 15 December 2022
Baby G
DR DAVID HARKNESS (recalled)
Examination-in-chief by MR ASTBURY
Cross-examination by MR MYERS
Re-examination by MR ASTBURY
Thursday, 15 December 2022
(In the absence of the jury)
I'm not sure where Mr Astbury and Mr Driver have gone to. I know Mr Astbury is about to call Dr Harkness.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Oh right. So he's important then?
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: I need him here to make any progress, I'm afraid.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: (Pause)
I wonder whether I could just go outside.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Certainly.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: (Pause)
The witness, unfortunately, is still in the witness room.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: So I gather, but he's now on his way.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Right. You know more than I do.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Well, I've just enquired.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: (Pause)
(In the presence of the jury)
Sorry you have been kept waiting.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: I recall Dr David Harkness, please.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: DR DAVID HARKNESS (recalled)
Examination-in-chief by MR ASTBURY
Dr Harkness, you have given evidence before on a number of occasions but could you just introduce yourself again for the purpose of the record, please?
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes, I'm Dr David Ian Harkness.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: You gave evidence most recently in respect of a baby by the name of [Baby G] and your contact with [Baby G] on and around 7 September 2015.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: I'm going to ask you some questions about your contact with the same baby on 21 September 2015.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: You told us last time you have some memory of [Baby G] because she was in the unit for some time and you had contact with her, as a consequence, on more than one or two occasions. But dealing specifically with the 21st, do you recall what shift you were on on that date?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Not particularly, not without looking at the notes.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: I was on a day shift and I was on the neonatal unit, but whether I was there all day or just came across for that -- for this episode...
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: So what hours would that shift have been?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Starting at 8.30, finishing at 4.30.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: Do you remember anything about the ward that particular day?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: All right. Was it particularly busy?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I can't remember.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: You have had the medical notes in an attempt to refresh your memory for those sorts of reasons and I think it's right that you have not expressly made any notes in respect of [Baby G] on that day.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: But you did recognise your handwriting on a particular form?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: So I'm going to ask Mr Murphy, please, to go to tile 71 and the document behind it, please.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Is this the form upon which you recognised your handwriting?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: Is it the entry in the first row, dated 21 September?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: Just to be clear then, can you identify the date, the writing, is that you, 21/9/15?
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: Circling -- obviously a circle is a circle. Then "left foot" is your writing?
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: "Dr Gibbs", your writing.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: "7th attempt by multiple staff"?
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: So it's all yours?
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: Thank you, good.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Just casting your mind back, if you can, you have mentioned multiple staff. Were you aware of who first attempted to cannulate [Baby G] that particular day?
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: Were you aware that Dr Chang had attempted to cannulate?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Only from looking through the notes.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: All right. The fact that Dr Gibbs became involved, does that suggest others attempted to cannulate [Baby G]?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes, and potentially I tried myself as well and called Dr Gibbs. I can't recollect exactly, but typically it'll be an SHO that will start, followed by a registrar, and if the registrars feel they are unable to, then we call the consultant.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: The fact that you filled this form in, does that suggest that you were present when Dr Gibbs finally succeeded?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: Do you have any recollection of being with Dr Gibbs during the course of this procedure?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Vaguely.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: I'm going to ask you, please, to do your best to remember as much detail as you can. Have you often attempted cannulation with Dr Gibbs?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Possibly one or two other occasions, but not that I can think of, no.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: Okay. We can see from the form that the site in the end was the left foot; is that correct?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: Do you recall there being attempts to cannulate in other locations?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: There would have been, yes, but I can't remember exactly where.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: Were you assisting Dr Gibbs?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: And how were you assisting Dr Gibbs?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I would have been there to hold limbs, to make it easier for him to cannulate and keep the baby still. But also I would have been there to give a kind of sugar water as pain relief and also to pass him the equipment that he needed to secure a cannula.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: We've heard that's often the duty of the designated nurse or a nurse who is available. Do you recall why you ended up with that particular job that day?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I expect the nurses were very busy, but I can't be specific why.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: Okay. Casting your mind back, can you remember which room this took place in?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I believe it was room 2.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: Can you remember whether anyone else was with you while you were attempting to cannulate with Dr Gibbs?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I can't remember.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: Do you remember whereabouts in room 2 this was taking place?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I believe on the right-hand side, but I could be mistaken.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: All right. We've heard there was a screen in place. Do you recall the screen?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: We typically put a screen around the babies if there's other -- particularly if there's other parents in the room or we think parents are visiting, then we'll use a screen.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: And do you remember where or more specifically upon what or within what [Baby G] was placed whilst cannulation was being attempted?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I think we used a kind of table type set-up, which has got a soft mattress that can go up and down, to do it, I think, or it may very well have been in the cot.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: I can't remember which one we did at the time.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: Okay, all right. Do you recall at that time [Baby G] was ordinarily in a cot as opposed to an incubator?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: Do you remember what time roughly this was taking place?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I think the afternoon, but that's all about I remember.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: And do you remember any nurses being in the room whilst this was going on?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Not that I can remember, no.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: Have you had the opportunity this morning to refresh your memory from the statement that you provided?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: I think that was dated, let me just check, 14 September 2018. Did your statement help you with any nurses that may have been present?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I think [Nurse B] -- I can't pronounce her surname properly -- was in the vicinity, but how close to us I can't remember.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: Do you actually have a recollection of that nurse being in the room or is that based on your statement?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: That's based on my statement.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: Okay. Do you recall any other nurses in the room?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: No, that was all I remember at that point in time.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: All right. Do you remember how long you were attempting to cannulate [Baby G]?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I think it still took a couple of attempts. I think it would have been a good 15 minutes or so, I would have -- as a rough estimate.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: Do you recall whether [Baby G] had any monitoring attached to her?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes, she was on, I think, a Masimo monitor -- it may have been a Philips monitor -- that was attached to one of her limbs.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: Do you happen to remember which limb?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: During the course of trying more than one site, do you recall if it had to be moved at all?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I can't recall.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: Would that ordinarily happen in those sort of circumstances?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Depending on which limbs we thought were the best limbs to try, you would occasionally move it from one limb to another. You'd move it from one limb to a different limb, make
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: sure you've got a good trace before you move on, would be typically what you'd do.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: Is there any reason why you make sure the monitor is receiving a good trace when you move it?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: They can be quite -- the trace can be -- if it's not quite in the right place will not show you accurately what the baby is doing, so if it's a hand or a leg, you want to make sure that you know that the heart rate is there and the saturations are there before you move on, otherwise it can be falsely reassuring.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: Okay. Would you consider it important to keep the monitor on --
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: -- and attached in those circumstances?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: Do you have any recollection of switching either the alarm or the monitor on or off at any stage?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I definitely wouldn't have turned it off. Silencing the alarm is quite easy to do and as part of de-stressing the situation we will silence the alarm, but that only goes on for a matter of seconds to a minute. But I definitely wouldn't have turned the monitor off.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: Why's that?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: It's not safe. In fact, I'm not even sure if I know how to turn off the particular monitors. But at no point would I have turned the monitor off.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: Okay. Do you recall, once cannulation had been successful, what you did next?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I can't remember. I think I probably informed the designated nurse or a nurse in the vicinity and then documented in the notes that we've had the seven attempts, as in the notes there.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: You provide two alternatives there. Either the designated nurse or another nurse. What's the protocol in that regard?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Ideally, the designated nurse because you would know that they are going to attend to that patient and that's their
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: designated role for the day. However, if the designated nurse is busy, then you would want to inform a different nurse to make sure that the team were aware and that they would then be able to look after the baby.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: Do you have any recollection from that occasion of who you told or at what stage you told them that?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Not particularly, no.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: Do you have any recollection of actually leaving [Baby G] once the cannulation was complete?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I remember leaving the room to document. Other than that I can't remember any more about that particular moment.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: I think in preparation for your statement you went on to check the notes and observed that after this you're aware that [Baby G] was moved into nursery 1.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: What is -- having had such difficulty cannulating the baby in these sort of circumstances, what would your view of that successful cannulation be?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: In what respect, sorry?
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: Well, is there a particular practice of yours where, in these sort of circumstances, cannulation succeeds, is it something to be taken care of, is it something to be protected? What's your view in the aftermath of cannulation?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I mean, all cannulas come with a certain degree of difficulty and pressures. Everyone has different ways of securing a cannula, but in these cases you certainly like to make sure that the nurses are fully aware. The way that you secure, the way you protect it, you might be a little more careful, but my typical practice is I look after them all the same because I'd rather them not be replaced.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: When you talk about protecting and securing them, what sort of steps does that involve?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: So we use what we call Steri-Strips or the butterfly sutures to wrap around the cannula. We then use clear dressings over the cannula as well. Quite often we have what we call a baby board, which is a rigid splint that you put on the hand for the baby to hold. And depending on where you're working at the time, I can't remember in Chester, you also wrap bandages around the area to secure it as well. So multiple, three or four
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: different layers of securing the cannula and then it's making sure that it's not pulled in and out of babygros or anything that could dislodge it.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: And those efforts to secure the cannula, are they part of the cannulation process for the doctor or is that where the nurse comes in and takes over and does that sort of thing?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Up until the bandaging -- typically the doctors -- the bandaging can be the doctor, can be the nurse. Quite variable, but when it comes to the Steri-Strips, the see-through dressings, the doctors will do that bit.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: Possibly with, if there's not two doctors, the assistance of a nurse, but typically the control of that situation is by the doctor.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: It's having reached that stage that you'd alert the nurse in circumstances such as this where there isn't a nurse present?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: You told us you can't recall where you went after the cannulation succeeded. Do you remember how much of your shift was left at that stage?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: I don't, no.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: Do you remember having any conversations with anyone about events following the cannulation?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Not particularly. I think looking at the notes, there was a deterioration, but I can't remember anything more than that very vague recollection.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: So from the notes you've seen that there was a deterioration after you had finished cannulating. I'm just wondering if you have any personal recollection of any conversations with anybody about the cannulation itself.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Other than speaking to nursing staff and ensuring that they knew it had happened, I can't remember anything further than that.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: All right. I have no more questions. But if you could wait there, please.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Cross-examination by MR MYERS
Just dealing with that last point first, please, you just said that other than speaking to nursing staff that it had happened, you don't remember any other conversation.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: You said that was a memory that you have. Could Dr Harkness be shown a copy of his statement at page 1926? Page 7 of 7. This is for Dr Harkness and his Lordship and the lawyers.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: If you look at the top paragraph there, Dr Harkness, when you made your statement in September 2018, what you actually said on this issue was:
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: "I do not remember speaking to a nurse, but I am sure I would have identified who was the designated nurse and informed them. It is very unlikely I would have informed anyone else other than the designated nurse."
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Right? So in fact, you don't have -- when you wrote that statement you didn't have a memory of speaking to a nurse.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: I think from looking through my statement again just a very vague recollection, but, as I've said, I can't specify who it would have been. I expected it was the designated nurse.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: Do you agree it says:
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: "I do not remember speaking to a nurse, but I am sure I would have identified who [the nurse was]"?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: Thank you very much. That's the statement for the time being, Mr Murphy. We may go back.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Just for the purposes of clarity we know this procedure took place in nursery 4, not nursery 2. [Baby G] was on a treatment trolley when it took place, wasn't she?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes. Like I said, that was what my thought would have been, but I couldn't have been sure.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: You're not too clear, is this right, as to whether screens were put up or not?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: And you do remember [Nurse B] being there at various points?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: With regard to cannula insertion, is it right that normally you would hope to have a cannula insertion achieved within two to three attempts?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Normally, yes.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: Seven attempts is a lot, isn't it?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: It would take a good deal longer than 15 minutes for seven attempts to be made, wouldn't it?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Sorry, that was a reference to Dr Gibbs' attempts, not all the attempts.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: All right. Just so we're clear, 10 to 15 minutes might cover just one or two attempts; do you agree?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: So if there had been seven attempts this has gone on for some time with [Baby G], hasn't it?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Potentially, yes.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: Do you recall the monitor being detached as the procedure was being performed? Do you recall that happening at any point?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: Do you recall the monitor being switched off as the procedure was performed?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: And you've actually said that wouldn't happen.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: Now, at the end of a procedure like this, the things that should happen are as follows -- and you tell me if this is right.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: The baby should be placed back in a cot.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Sometimes they are left on the trolley until the nurse comes, because it has cot sides, but otherwise they're put back in their cot.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: In your statement you said [Baby G] would have been placed back in the cot.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: At some point briefly afterwards.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: That should happen, shouldn't it?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Like I said, they can be left on the trolley but most of the time they are put back into the cot.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: The screen should be removed, shouldn't it?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: The designated nurse, or at least another nurse, should be told that the procedure has finished, isn't that right?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: If the monitor had been removed at any point it should be reattached by then?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: It shouldn't be removed, but yes it would have been reattached.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: And if it had been switched off, and we recognise you say it wouldn't have been, but if it had been it should certainly be switched back on before the baby is left?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: I'm going to suggest, Dr Harkness, that when you and Dr Gibbs left [Baby G], you left her without her being placed back in the cot; do you agree that's possible?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Possible, but no recollection.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: You left without removing the screens from around there; could that have happened?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: No recollection, but potentially.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: I'm going to suggest the monitor had been turned off and you both left without it being turned on.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: And you both left without telling [Nurse B], or anybody, that you had finished. Isn't that what happened?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: I don't think so, no. That's highly unlikely.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: It would be a serious error to leave a baby on its own, on her own, behind a screen without the monitor turned on and not having told the nurse that you had finished, wouldn't it?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: I'm going to suggest, Dr Harkness, that some time after you had finished this procedure, a little later that day, both you and Dr Gibbs spoke to [Nurse B] to apologise for how [Baby G] had been left.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: I can't remember.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: You can't remember?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: You would remember, surely, if there had been a conversation with an apology for leaving a baby unattended after numerous attempts to cannulate with the monitor switched off, wouldn't you?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: It was 2015. I can't remember.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: Is that not something that would stand out?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: In -- no.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: It's not a regular occurrence, is it?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: It's not a regular occurrence, but with the passage of time and lots of things happening since then, I can't remember.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: I'm going to suggest, Dr Harkness, that you and Dr Gibbs together spoke to [Nurse B] in the corridor outside nursery 4 to apologise.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: I can't remember.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: You apologised, both there together, for not having told her that you had finished with [Baby G]; isn't that what happened?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: I still can't remember.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: You apologised for leaving her behind the screen without anyone being told, didn't that happen?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: I still can't remember.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: And you apologised for failing to switch the monitor back on.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Once again, I can't remember.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: You must know very well, Dr Harkness, that took place.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: I can't remember.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: When you finished with [Baby G], you went back to the paediatric ward to complete a handover, didn't you?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: I can't remember. I haven't got the exact time documented, so it depended on what time of day that was.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: Could Dr Harkness be shown his statement at page 1925, please? If we go down that page, five lines up from the bottom, the penultimate paragraph.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: That would have been based on looking at the clinical notes and the times documented by other doctors.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: You say:
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: "I, after handing over to a nurse, went straight over to the paediatric ward to complete the handover."
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Didn't you?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: If that's what I've written and that's what the notes --
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: And you were in a rush -- sorry, Dr Harkness, what did you say?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: I said that would have been based on the timings in the clinical notes and a typical working day.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: Yes. And you were in a rush to get elsewhere after you'd finished with [Baby G], weren't you?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: I would not say that we rushed to handover, no.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: And you left [Baby G] without the monitor on, behind a screen, without telling anybody?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Not that I remember.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: And you went back to apologise later?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Not that I remember.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: I suggest a detail like that is not something you would forget.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: I disagree.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: Re-examination by MR ASTBURY
Just put the statement back up, please.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Dr Harkness, you were taken initially to the top of page 7 in your statement:
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "I don't remember speaking to a nurse."
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: You can see that at the very top of the page?
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: But in the preceding paragraph, from the page before, you did recall handing over to a nurse.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: It reads:
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: "I, after handing over to a nurse, went straight to the paediatric ward to complete the handover"; yes?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: Okay. So presumably, correct me if I'm wrong, there would have been some conversation with the nurse to whom you handed over?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: And I wonder, please, if Mr Murphy could assist with page K5596 on the screen. If we can put up that particular page.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: We've heard from other witnesses, can you confirm it, that the witness statement that we've been referring to is actually prepared from an interview that takes place, which is recorded and it's transcribed verbatim and it's from that which somebody then prepares the witness statement?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: So if we just go -- if we look on that page just below halfway, we can see 3358, okay. Can you see that line?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: And I'd just like to take you through what then follows and confirm if that is an accurate recollection of yours with the qualification that it includes.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: This is you:
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: "So he'd just done the cannula."
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Presumably that's Dr Gibbs, is it?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: "Answer: I would have then got the notes to write in and said to the nurse.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: "Question: Okay, do you remember saying that to the nurse?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: "Answer: I can't say I'm 100%, but looking at the nurse that was on, I'm sure I would have said to her straightaway, let's get things -- let's get the cannula, because again there was concerns that we'd not had the fluids running, so I'm pretty sure that I did, but I can't be 100%.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: "Question: Let's have a look through these notes again.
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: "Answer: Have you got the drug charts? They're the best indication of when it then started."
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: So at the time of your interview with the police, which was a little before the statement was signed, was that, to the best of your recollection, what happened with the nurse after you'd finished?
blocks.speaker: ASTBURY

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: HARKNESS

blocks.text: Thank you.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: I have to say, my Lord, that's the best recollection of "what would have happened with the nurse", is the wording in the statement -- the interview, sorry.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: I have nothing further. Does my Lord have any questions?
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: I don't, thank you very much.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Thank you, Dr Harkness. That completes your evidence today. Exactly the same instructions apply as hitherto: no discussion with anyone about anything to do with this case. Thank you very much.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: (The witness withdrew)

My Lord, it's very early for a break, but there is something I need to discuss with Mr Myers which, for reasons that your Lordship knows -- there are events going on in another court first thing this morning...
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: It is very early for a break, it's only half an hour afterwards, but I'm afraid there's nothing more we can do at this stage because Mr Johnson and Mr Myers need to speak. It's difficult to know how long this is going to take.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Perhaps if the jury at least get time to have a cup of tea without burning their lips.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Yes. Don't feel that it's only going to be 10 minutes, in other words, it might be longer. So take your time and if you're not ready and we're ready then we'll wait for you. All right? Thank you very much.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: (In the absence of the jury)
Because it's not known how long this is going to be, I'm just thinking of the situation of Ms Letby, whether she should be taken back down.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: I think that's probably a good idea because what Mr Myers and I discuss may involve him wishing to speak to Ms Letby as well.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Which would need to be downstairs?
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Exactly.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Could you take Ms Letby downstairs, please, because this may be longer than 10 minutes, we just don't know. Thank you.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: (Pause)
Thank you. I'll rise then.
(Adjournment)
Jury in, please.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: (In the presence of the jury)

My apologies, members of the jury, for that break being a lot longer than I thought it was going to be. In fact, I have a further apology to make to you, and it is this, that we are not going to be able to hear any further evidence in this trial before we have our break tomorrow. So in other words, this is going to be the end of the trial at this stage before the three-week break. So it means you will be finishing today rather than probably this time tomorrow or even earlier tomorrow than would otherwise have been the case for reasons that I needn't concern you with. They don't concern you, but there are reasons why we can't proceed.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: So we are now going to embark upon the longest break yet that there has been during the course of this trial.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: You should still have the original document that you were provided with in relation to your responsibilities as a juror together with my typed note highlighting those responsibilities. They will now be well embedded in your minds, I have no doubt, because I've been reminding you continuously of those responsibilities.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: You will make decisions in this case in due course on all the evidence that you hear and obviously there is a lot more evidence to hear in this case. So do not have any settled opinions about what your ultimate decision is going to be. Reserve your judgement until the end of the case.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Do not, most importantly, discuss this case with anybody. You are not going to be together again until we reassemble on Monday, 9 January 2023 to resume this case, so you must not talk to anyone, obviously, about it. Keep your thoughts to yourselves and do not communicate in any way with anyone or conduct any research by any means about anything or anyone to do with this case. This is vitally important and must be obeyed until the very end of the trial. All right?
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: It sounds repetitive, pedantic, but it is just so important in any case, not least of course in this one.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: All right? So thank you very much for your patience and your diligence and attendance to date. I wish you a happy Christmas
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: and I look forward to seeing you on Monday, 9 January next year. Until that point, do other things, think about other things.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: (In the absence of the jury)

Mr Johnson and Mr Myers, I know that there is work to be done now. I shall be available this afternoon and tomorrow if I am needed for the court to convene to deal with any matters. Should it be the case that it is quite apparent that there need not be a listing of this case tomorrow -obviously the jury will not be involved at any hearing, but should that be the case would you please inform the court or the Listing Office that the case need not be listed?
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: The default position is the case will be listed at 10.30 tomorrow unless you indicate otherwise.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: We understand, my Lord. Thank you.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: You understand that. Thank you very much.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: If the case is to be listed tomorrow, I'll leave it to you as to whether the defendant is required to be brought here or not, but that will obviously need to be known by the prison staff.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: We shall deal with that too, my Lord, thank you.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: I'll leave that to you as before, Mr Myers. Thank you very much indeed.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: As I say, I shall be available from probably about 2.15-ish this afternoon if necessary. Thank you very much indeed.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Ms Letby, Mr Myers, I have no doubt, will be coming down to speak to you and your legal team. Ms Letby should not be taken from this building until Mr Myers or Mr Maher indicate that --
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Yes, thank you, my Lord.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: (Inaudible: no microphone).
blocks.speaker: DOCK OFFICER

blocks.text: She can't have a visit before 2 o'clock?
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: That's fine. Just so we know what the situation is.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: There you are, Mr Myers.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: We'll be able to see Ms Letby this afternoon if that's the case. As long as we're all still here.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: Thank you.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: Thank you very much indeed.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: (The court adjourned until a time and date to be determined)
